collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: The rains have uncovered old bones in the stream bank: study them and rebury them, or cover them again now.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: After the heavy rains, part of the stream bank has washed away, and old bones are showing in the earth: a person, buried a very long time ago, with a necklace of shells and a small stone tool beside them. (subject) wants to study them carefully before anything is moved. (friend) wants them covered again right away, with respect.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They agree on a middle way. (subject) looks carefully but doesn't take anything away: the way the person was laid, the shells, the tool. (subject.He/she) draws it all on bark. Then they rebury the person together, a little higher up, safe from the stream. (friend) says a few words. (subject) keeps the drawing, and says it tells them something about the people who were here before.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) gives way. (friend) and (subject.he/she) cover the bones again with fresh earth and stones, so the stream can't reach them. (friend) speaks quietly over the grave. (subject) is a little sad about all the things they'll never know. But (subject.he/she) also feels that whoever it was would rather be left in peace than drawn on bark. They walk home without talking.
